content.text: A rainy night at a CTA bus stop · Lawrence & Western, Lincoln Square, Chicago · late 1993
World board + footage library · counter-world: steel / time-lapse · building live
Lincoln Square, Chicago, 1993. Southbound #49 Western stop at Lawrence. 24-hour Owl route; #81 Lawrence crosses; Western Brown Line a block east.
Blue hour gives way to high-pressure sodium. Storefront fluorescents, Davis Theater neon, brake lights in wet asphalt.
Drizzle on glass, rings in puddles, spray off tires, beads on a bus shelter roof. Texture plates, period-neutral.
CTA's 1991 Flxible Metro: white body with a red-and-blue stripe, flip-dot destination sign, kneeling hiss, fare box clatter.
CTA bus-stop sign on a pole, shelter ads, newspaper boxes (Tribune, Sun-Times, Reader), alley lights, Jewel and Walgreens signs.
Brick three-flats, bungalows, German storefronts on Lincoln, L structure, the Davis marquee.
Starter jackets, Bulls caps, long wool coats, Walkmans, umbrellas that don't quite work.
Hi8 and VHS camcorder: date stamp, auto-iris breathing, smeared highlights, handheld from the curb. 16mm for the counter-world.
Palette pulled from the footage by k-means, not picked by eye.
CTA sans-serif signage, flip-dot destination matrix, TV-news chyron, Accu-Weather graphics.
Rain on the shelter, the bus's air brakes and kneel, wet tires, a radio in a passing car.
Local TV anchors and forecasters, CTA announcements, neighborhood talk.
Bulls three-peat (June 20, 1993), Richard M. Daley's first full term, CTA service cuts and the Green Line shutdown (1994).
Heavy industry, How It's Made spirit. Molten orange rhymes with sodium; sparks rhyme with rain; furnace roar rhymes with the bus hiss.
Compressed time against a stopped moment. Blooms, clouds, seasons. Dew rhymes with rain; the sun's arc rhymes with headlights.
Printing presses, bioluminescence: a few strange cousins for the cut.
Chicago clip beside its counter twin, chosen from the catalog on shared tags. One line on why they cut.
Every catalog clip, binned by dominant color family; sub-rows by direction and pace.
Measured motion energy, from near-static to high-velocity. Chicago lane over counter-world lane.

A 25-minute onboard audio recording of an ex-1995 CTA Flxible Metro (TransitHubChicago, YouTube 2022): diesel idle, the kneel hiss, door chime, the air-brake sigh at every stop. REF only.
The WBBM-TV Channel 2 5:30 news, Dec 12 1993: the Accu-Weather segment calls the rain for tonight. Our evening is literally on the forecast. Clip in this zone.

Shoot on 16mm or Betacam SP. Use long lenses across Western, with rain falling between lens and subject. Lock off a wide on the shelter and let the bus wipe the frame L→R. Inside the bus, fluorescent green-white; outside, sodium orange. Handheld only for the "news" voice.
Upper- and lowercase Helvetica became the CTA sign face with the 1969–70 Dan Ryan/Kennedy signage, and the agency's de facto corporate type. Before that: mostly Futura caps.
Feb 21 1993: the Ravenswood officially becomes the Brown Line. New color-coded roller curtains on the cars, though riders keep saying "the Ravenswood". Type on the board can carry both names.

The bus speaks in dot-matrix caps: amber or yellow-green dots on black, readable through rain. Use a mono or dot face, all caps, wide tracking. On screen it should flicker slightly when the dots flip.

Condensed bold sans on beveled gradient bars, drop shadows, "ACCU-WEATHER" lockups. Reference: the WBBM-TV Dec 12 1993 and WLS-TV May 18 1993 tapes in VOICE. REF only, do not reproduce the station marks.
The Davis Theater's vertical stacked letters (see ARCHITECTURE): tall caps, one letter per cell, read top to bottom. Halation in the rain is part of the letterform.

Score direction: sparse, one sustained synth pad under the rain, nothing on the beat until the bus arrives.
Furnace roar matches the bus's diesel idle. Spark crackle matches rain on the roof. The ladle pour matches the brake hiss. Time-lapse sections go near-silent, just room tone and a clock.
VHS hiss, wow and flutter, the head-switch click at a cut. Mono. The news tapes in VOICE carry exactly this.
Flat, clipped call-outs: "Lawrence. Lawrence and Western." Before automated announcements, the driver calls the stop, or doesn't. Sound check: the Flxible recording in SOUND.

North Side Chicago: the flattened "a" (Western, Lawrence), news-anchor neutral on TV, neighbors in Polish, Korean, Spanish and German at the corner. Lincoln Square still carried its German shopfronts in 1993.
